children: reported positive late-stage clinical results for its eczema treatment Ebglyss, potentially expanding the drug's commercial opportunity into a difficult-to-treat form of atopic dermatitis affecting the hands and feet. The Phase 3 success strengthens Lilly's immunology portfolio as the pharmaceutical giant seeks to broaden its growth beyond its blockbuster obesity and diabetes treatments.

Ebglyss, developed and marketed in partnership with Spanish pharmaceutical company Almirall, is an injectable antibody therapy already approved in the U.S. and other major markets for patients aged 12 and older with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis under specified treatment conditions.
The latest Phase 3 ADtouch study evaluated Ebglyss 250 mg against placebo in 221 adults and adolescents with moderate-to-severe hand-and-foot eczema over 16 weeks.
According to topline results released Wednesday,
53% of patients receiving Ebglyss achieved clear or almost clear skin on their hands and feet
, compared with 27% in the placebo group.
The 26-percentage-point difference means patients receiving Lilly's treatment were nearly twice as likely to meet the study's primary endpoint.
Importantly, the company reported no new safety signals, with the treatment's safety profile remaining consistent with previous clinical findings.
Lilly has already shared the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, seeking a label update to specifically include moderate-to-severe hand-and-foot atopic dermatitis.
The findings were also selected for presentation at the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology Congress in Vienna this week.
For investors, the next catalyst is whether the FDA accepts the additional clinical evidence and grants the requested label expansion.
A successful update could strengthen Ebglyss's competitive positioning by providing physicians with specific Phase 3 evidence for treating persistent eczema affecting the hands and feet.
Investors should also watch the full ADtouch data presentation, including secondary efficacy outcomes, treatment consistency and detailed safety results.

Although the development represents a clinical milestone, its financial impact will ultimately depend on regulatory approval, physician adoption and whether broader prescribing translates into meaningful additional sales.

title: Eli Lilly Scores Major Win for Key Eczema Drug
